title: Bhishma's honest answer
hook: the Pandavas ask their own grandsire how he can be killed, and he tells them the truth
carry: satya: truth is dharma, even against yourself
tomorrow: why won't Bhishma fight Shikhandi, of all people?

segments.voice: Yesterday Krishna leapt from the chariot and ran at Bhishma on foot, a God who bends for his devotees, and Bhishma welcomed him. Your line: bhakta vatsala: god bends for his devotees. And the old man is still standing.
screen: `KRISHNA RUNS AT BHISHMA.` · `GOD BENDS FOR HIS DEVOTEES.` · `STILL STANDING.`

segments.voice: Night, and the Pandava camp is quiet in the wrong way. Another day has gone to Bhishma, the commander of the other side and the elder these brothers grew up calling grandsire. Yudhishthira can't see a way through. Then he remembers the first morning, when he walked over to Bhishma unarmed. Bhishma promised him counsel then, and told him to ask another time how he could be beaten. So the brothers set their weapons aside, and with Krishna they walk across the dark field to the enemy's tent.
screen: `ANOTHER DAY LOST TO BHISHMA.` → `A PROMISE OF COUNSEL.` → `ACROSS THE FIELD AT NIGHT.`

segments.voice: Bhishma doesn't reach for a sword. In Ganguli's English, he welcomes them. Yudhishthira asks it out loud: how can you be defeated? And Bhishma answers. As long as he holds his bow, no one can bring him down. But there is a warrior he will not fight. Shikhandi, Drupada's child, was born a daughter, and Bhishma has vowed never to raise a weapon against one he counts as a woman. Put Shikhandi in front, he tells them, and let Arjuna shoot from behind. Walking back, Arjuna comes apart. He remembers climbing into Bhishma's lap as a boy and calling him father, and Bhishma gently correcting him: not your father, child, your father's father. How can I kill him? It's the same grief that opens the Bhagavad Gita, where Arjuna asks how he can aim arrows at Bhishma and Drona, men he should worship. Now the teaching. In Hinduism, truth, satya, sits at the heart of dharma. Bhishma's whole life is built on keeping his word; two days ago you met the Bhishma pratigya, a vow that binds for life. Tonight his truthfulness costs him his life. But the epic won't make him simple. The same loyalty to his vow keeps him on the wrong side of this war. Dharma, the Mahabharata keeps saying, is subtle.
screen: `HOW CAN YOU BE DEFEATED?` · `SHIKHANDI IN FRONT` · `A BOY IN HIS GRANDSIRE'S LAP` · then, large: `SATYA: TRUTH IS DHARMA`

segments.voice: Sit tall and let your breath settle. Hindu students have long heard a teacher's charge from the Taittiriya Upanishad: satyam vada, dharmam chara. Speak the truth; walk in dharma. Breathing in, say satyam vada silently. Breathing out, dharmam chara. Then bring to mind one true thing you've been putting off saying, and just hold it for a moment. If you pray, offer it in your prayer. If you don't, let it be a quiet resolve.
Bhishma's fall. Tonight it begins with a question asked in his own tent, and an honest answer that he gives against himself.
Your line: satya: truth is dharma, even against yourself. Bhishma gave the answer that would end him. That's day eight hundred twenty-seven.

howItsDone: Retellings of the Mahabharata keep the night when the Pandavas visit Bhishma's tent and he tells them how he can be overcome, and in Hindi an unbreakable promise is still called a 'Bhishma pratigya'.

myth: the Pandavas went to Bhishma's tent to attack him in the dark

Hindus honor him for keeping his word at any cost; the epic also shows that the same vow kept him on the wrong side. that's why it calls dharma subtle.

fork.setup: you're Bhishma. you promised the Pandavas counsel. now they ask the one question whose true answer will kill you. what does satya ask of you?
options: tell them plainly: put Shikhandi in front.
give a vague answer; technically you kept your promise.
refuse; a promise made to the other side doesn't count.
fork.reveal: Bhishma tells them plainly. for him, satya isn't truth when it's convenient; a kept word is the backbone of dharma.

original.note: truth; for Hindus, one of the pillars of dharma.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Pandavas found Bhishma's weak spot.
what it means: Bhishma gave them his weak spot himself, because he'd promised counsel and wouldn't lie.
what a scholar hears: Bhishma's truthfulness and his vow are his greatness and his trap at once: the epic's way of saying dharma is subtle.

chat.says: dad's making us watch the old Mahabharata on weekends 😭 Sam asked why everyone treats Bhishma like a hero when he's literally on the bad side. wait, why??
options: he never broke his word, even when the truth meant his own death. that's satya.
he was the strongest fighter, and in the epic strength is what makes a hero.
he was secretly fighting for the Pandavas the whole time.
chat.meaning: Asked how he could be beaten, Bhishma told the Pandavas the truth that would end him. Hindus honor that satya, while the epic admits his vow also bound him to the wrong side.

Drupada.meaning: the king who is Shikhandi's father

Yudhishthira.meaning: the eldest Pandava, who asks Bhishma the hard question

Pandava.meaning: a son of Pandu; one of the five brothers

satya.meaning: truth; a heart of dharma in Hindu teaching
